messages:
sam (eng-infra): noticing increased gRPC stalls on large model streaming between pods in us-west-2. flagging because it looks like chunked requests hang mid-stream and then the client retries lots -> backpressure on the runtime. :frowning:
izzy (netops): which nodes? any pattern by AZ or instance type?
maria (sre): seeing same SPC: pod egress packet retransmits spike on nodes gpu-pool-3-{12,14,20}. tcpdump shows lots of 'frag' and 'bad checksum' after heavy 16KB-ish writes from the model server.
luke (runtime): we stream tokens in ~4KB frames but kernel offloads may coalesce into oversized segments. could be GSO/GRO + overlay MTU mismatch causing IP fragmentation and then reassembly stalls.
jen (eng): reproducer: run a 50MB stream over a GRPC bidi stream between two pods on different nodes in same AZ. 80% chance it stalls after ~12-20s. small streams unaffected.
izzy (netops): I ran path MTU check across the overlay and the VPC path: host MTU is 9001 on hosts (we enable jumbo on instance ENIs), but our VXLAN tunnel MTU is 1450 in CNI config? wait that mismatch seems weird. can you paste `ip link` and `ip route` from one node?
maria (sre): pasted snippets:```
$ ip link show vxlan0
4: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ ip link show ens5
2: ens5: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP,MULTICAST> mtu 9001 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
jen (eng): aha so host NIC MTU 9001, overlay vxlan 1450. that should avoid fragmentation at tunnel level, but what about GSO/GRO? kernel might be coalescing 64K segments and VxLAN tries to encapsulate then the ENI path can't handle the oversized inner packet -> fragmentation on wire.
izzy (netops): ran tcpdump on host and on pod veth. saw that pod's veth emits large LSO segments (e.g. 64KB), host encapsulates to VxLAN, but underneath the ENI drops fragments when outer packet >1500 because some middle path (AWS transit/gbps) doesn't accept jumbo for tunneled frames. the reassembly seems to happen asynchronously and kernel user of gRPC socket waits for reassembled packet which stalls the stream.
luke (runtime): this matches a known GSO/GRO interaction with gRPC streaming where downstream expects ordered chunks; when a segment is dropped or reassembly delays, the gRPC transport stalls and the runtime holds token generation, causing queue depth to blow up.
maria (sre): quick mitigation that worked on test nodes: `ethtool -K vxlan0 gso off gro off tso off` on host vxlan interface -> immediate drop in retransmits and no more stalls for large streams. but disabling offloads increases CPU on host network path. :grimacing:
jen (eng): other options? lower MTU on pod network so host never sees large coalesced segments? e.g. set pod mtu to 1200 or 1400 in CNI manifest and roll cluster.
izzy (netops): we can do pod-MTU 1400 as config change in CNI. that is lower-impact than disabling offloads globally. also enabling `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` helps when path MTU blackholes exist. command: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`
luke (runtime): we should also consider kernel buglet: older kernels + ovs/vxlan had GRO offload reassembly ordering issues. nodes running 5.10 show higher failure; 5.15 nodes less so. we should schedule a canary kernel upgrade for one AZ.
maria (sre): checklist for rollout: 1) patch CNI to pod MTU=1400 in staging, 2) enable tcp_mtu_probing on hosts, 3) monitor gRPC stall rate and tx_retransmits, 4) if stable after 24h, roll prod. fallback is to disable GSO on vxlan for affected nodes during deploy.
izzy (netops): will open infra change PR to CNI and coordinate with infra-scheduler for a phased node reboot. estimate 3h of disruption if we misconfigure, but plan is zero-downtime if we cordon+drain GPUs.
jen (eng): any cost/perf implications? reducing pod MTU -> slightly higher per-packet CPU overhead but should be negligible vs the cost of stalled inference jobs. disabling offloads permanently would increase host CPU and could reduce GPU utilization.
luke (runtime): runtime can add a quick guard: detect long-lived gRPC streams with no progress and cut them to avoid queue buildup. but that's a bandaid; fixing MTU/offload mismatch is better.
maria (sre): created a short runbook in ops playbook: steps to detect (tcpdump pattern + `ss -tin` showing stalled ESTAB frames), mitigation commands (disable gso on vxlan, sysctl mtu probing), and rollback. linking in PR in infra repo. :white_check_mark:
nodewatcher-bot: Node gpu-pool-3-14 reported high netRxErr at 2026-10-12T14:21:10Z (auto alert)
sam (eng-infra): thanks all. action items: izzy -> CNI MTU PR, maria -> rollout runbook + monitor, luke -> runtime guard proposal. I'll follow up tomorrow and schedule kernel canary. :eyes:
